messages:
maria: Quick check before I open the TF PR — planning to change svc from ClusterIP -> NodePort to keep NLB TLS passthrough for /inference. Two quick Qs: (1) will `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` + NodePort preserve client IP and TLS passthrough? (2) how do we wire the Gateway API secret if the certs live in infra namespace but Gateway is in ingress namespace?

kyle: Short answers: (1) Yes, NodePort + externalTrafficPolicy: Local preserves client IP because traffic goes to node and gets forwarded to pod without SNAT. For TLS passthrough you also want NLB target group target_type = "ip" (not instance) and listener protocol = TCP so LB doesn't terminate TLS. Healthchecks are the common gotcha.

devon: Also +1 on target_type change. In TF you'll need to update aws_lb_target_group.target_type from "instance" -> "ip" and ensure health_check.port = "traffic-port" and protocol = "TCP" for passthrough. Example snippet:```hcl
resource "aws_lb_target_group" "inference" {
  name     = "inference-tg"
  port     = 443
  protocol = "TCP"
  target_type = "ip"
  health_check {
    port     = "traffic-port"
    protocol = "TCP"
  }
}
```

olivia: For the Gateway API secret question: you can use a SecretBinding resource to map a Secret in infra namespace to the Gateway namespace (depends on the gateway-controller, but contour/gatekeeper style controllers support it). If not supported, we need to duplicate the secret or move certs.

kyle: Exact wording: Gateway API uses a TLS certificateRef that must reference a Secret in the same namespace as the Gateway (for many controllers). SecretBinding (or a controller-specific resource) can reference a secret elsewhere and present it to the Gateway. If we can't use SecretBinding we should replicate the certs via automation.

maria: One more: will switching svc->NodePort break our canary? We have a canary svc (same port, different label selector) that lives alongside production.

devon: NodePort is per-service so k8s will assign different node ports unless you set `nodePort:` explicitly (or reuse the same one, which would conflict). Recommendation: let k8s auto-assign for prod, set explicit `nodePort` for the canary if you need stable mapping. Also check ClusterIP vs targetPort in the Pod spec — mismatch there is a common tf bug.

kyle: Small AWS gotcha: NLB health checks default to HTTP/80 if you accidentally leave the LB listener in HTTP mode. For TLS passthrough ensure listener is TCP/443 and health check uses TCP/traffic-port. If you intend ALB termination instead, switch to HTTPS listener and bind the cert on the LB (then Gateway secret is not used for TLS at the LB).

olivia: I can open the TF change: update target_type and health_check, plus add listener config. I'll include a note to copy cert to ingress namespace via automation if SecretBinding not available. Want a review from @maria and @devon before apply.

maria: :thumbsup: Please include Terraform plan in the PR and mark the change window (low traffic after 22:00 UTC). Also add a canary test using a mirrored service to validate TLS passthrough before full cutover.

deploy-bot: terraform plan: 3 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy — workspace=infra-prod — run_id=run-20260314-09

kyle: FYI add an annotation to the svc if you want the gateway-controller to skip cert injection: `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: tcp` and `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-protocol: tcp`. That keeps the LB behavior explicit.

maria: Perfect. I'll wait for the PR from olivia and will schedule the maintenance window. Thanks all.
